text:
Maya: Dropping the regional sweep summary for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints. Ran SSE, WebSocket streaming, and sync batched HTTP across us-west1 / eu-central1 / apac-sg on A100/H100/L4. TL;DR: streaming wins tail latency at low concurrency but non-streamed batched endpoints give better overall tokens/sec under high QPS.

Ajay: Nice — do you have numbers? and which kernel/runtime build? :eyes:

Maya: Paste of the csv we used (tokens/sec = avg throughput, p95 latency in ms):
```
region,gpu,endpoint,quant,throughput_tps,p95_ms
us-west1,A100,SSE,float16,420,62
us-west1,A100,WebSocket,float16,430,58
us-west1,A100,HTTP-batched,float16,1100,190
us-west1,H100,SSE,float16,760,48
us-west1,H100,WebSocket,float16,780,44
us-west1,H100,HTTP-batched,float16,2100,140
eu-central1,A100,SSE,int8,460,70
eu-central1,A100,HTTP-batched,int8,1200,210
apac-sg,L4,WebSocket,int8,520,95
apac-sg,L4,HTTP-batched,int8,1250,250
```

Maya: Kernel/runtime: flash-attn-v2 on H100, cutlass-direct for A100 FP16, and Triton-backed kernels for L4. Default runtime flags except we toggled continuous-batching window=20ms for the HTTP endpoints.

Sofia: Observations: flash-attn-v2 w/ H100 consistently reduced p95 by ~15-20ms for streaming endpoints vs A100 config. But batched HTTP still leverages larger batch sizes and wins throughput.

Liam: Also saw interesting behavior with quantization: int8 boosted tokens/sec by ~1.6x on A100 but increased jitter on p95 for streaming (spiky tail when KV-cache misses). Might be due to kernel fallback paths.

Cheng: Note about KV cache: streaming endpoints keep warm KV longer per-connection which helps when session stickiness is high. Batched HTTP loses reuse since requests are stateless and batching mixes different contexts — explains why throughput is higher but token cost per-context is higher.

Ajay: For capacity planning, how do you convert these into slot sizing? any simple rule?

Maya: Rough rule we used: pick target p95 SLAs first. If target p95 <= 100ms, prefer streaming on H100 and overprovision connections by ~20% for headroom. If target is throughput-driven (>1.5k tps), pick batched HTTP on H100/A100 with batch-window 15-30ms and scale replicas by ceil(target / single-rep-throughput). Example: if target 6000 tps in us-west1 on H100, single rep ~2100 -> need 3 replicas (3*2100=6300).

Sofia: One more wrinkle: WebSocket handshake and idle sockets bump memory (per-connection KV entries). For dense multi-tenant customers, we capped concurrent streaming connections per host to avoid OOM during long-lived sessions.

Maya: Small ascii tradeoff chart we sketched from the sweep (x=throughput, y=p95 latency):
```
   p95(ms)
   300 |     * HTTP-batched (A100)      * HTTP-batched (L4)
   200 |      * H1 batched(A100)       
   150 |         *                    
   100 |    * SSE (A100)    * WS (L4)
    50 | * SSE (H100) * WS (H100)      
       +--------------------------------
         0   500 1000 1500 2000 2500  tokens/sec
```

Ajay: Nice. Any kernel-level anomalies or misconfig flags to watch for?

Maya: Yes - two gotchas we hit:
1) On A100 FP16, enabling cutlass-wmma auto-tune gives slightly better throughput but breaks streaming latency due to extra kernel launch overhead for small token counts. Turn off auto-tune for low-latency streaming.
2) On L4 int8 paths, Triton kernel falls back to a reference kernel on rare token lengths leading to 500ms spikes. We filed infra ticket to guard fallback paths.

Cheng: Did you test continuous KV cache size (per-conn) vs batch-window tradeoff? curious numbers.

Maya: Quick micro-run: per-conn KV size 64 vs 256 tokens, on streaming throughput diff <5% but p95 improved ~10ms with larger KV for session reuse. For batched HTTP, larger KV no-op.

Liam: Any plan to expose recommendations in Console? Could map customer workload (sessions vs stateless QPS) to endpoint choice and recommended kernel flags.

Maya: Yep, prototype rule-set already in Optimize -> inference recommendations. Will sync with DevEx to make the UI hints clearer.
